authoredFrom: master spec 12b prepared Q&A, the seven demo beats, and the six registered rules of rules/ruleset-v1.0.json
reviewFlags: entry 2 (ICH M3 two-species phrasing) needs a toxicologist, not an engineer: is this how a reviewer actually opens that objection? It matters more than it looks, because this string is what live input is matched against at rungs 2 and 3.
entry 8 (a >100x in-vitro margin treated as an established exposure margin) needs a toxicologist.
entry 12 (clearing a Klimisch score on a QSAR claim as a category error) needs a toxicologist.

entries.challenge: the rat data shouldn't be discounted that hard
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R1, human relevance, so the rodent studies keep more of their stated confidence.

entries.challenge: ICH M3 asks for two species because rodent and non-rodent answer different questions. collapsing both into 'not human' throws that away
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R1, human relevance, so a two-species animal package is not discounted as one undifferentiated block.

entries.challenge: primary human hepatocytes are the whole point of the FDA roadmap. if anything R1 is too soft here
entries.paraphrase: Increase R1, human relevance, so human-cell evidence outweighs animal evidence more decisively.

entries.challenge: read-across from a known toxicophore is real evidence, you're treating it like noise
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R2, mechanistic proximity, so structural read-across is discounted less against a directly measured key event.

entries.challenge: why is a structural alert worth less than a cell assay? both are only proxies for a human liver
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R2, mechanistic proximity, on the grounds that structural and in-vitro evidence are both indirect.

entries.challenge: why does R3 only apply to negative findings? that looks convenient
entries.paraphrase: Turn R3, exposure relevance, off entirely, so a negative finding is not discounted for an unstated exposure margin.

entries.challenge: isn't the discounting just a fudge factor to get the answer you wanted
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R3, exposure relevance, so an unstated exposure margin costs a negative finding less weight.

entries.challenge: the in-vitro panel was run against clinical Cmax — a hundred-fold margin IS an exposure margin. stop calling it untested
entries.paraphrase: Record the in-vitro DILI panel as having an established exposure margin, so R3 stops discounting it.

entries.challenge: first-in-class orexin agonist. there is nothing like it in the training set — that QSAR call is out of domain
entries.paraphrase: Record the QSAR prediction as outside the model's applicability domain, so R4 admits it at reduced weight.

entries.challenge: a 0.5 downweight for out-of-domain is far too gentle. out of domain means the prediction is uninformative
entries.paraphrase: Increase R4, applicability domain, so an out-of-domain prediction is admitted at a much lower weight.

entries.challenge: klimisch 3 gets hammered too hard here. plenty of non-GLP work is perfectly sound
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R5, study reliability, so a Klimisch 3 study is not discounted so heavily.

entries.challenge: a klimisch score on a QSAR prediction is a category error. Klimisch grades experimental studies, not models
entries.paraphrase: Clear the Klimisch score on the QSAR prediction, so R5's reliability discount stops applying to a computational claim.

entries.challenge: cytotox and transporter both come out of Tox21. that's one platform, not two independent sources
entries.paraphrase: Reduce R6, concordance, so two readouts from one assay platform are not credited as two independent sources.
